## Before submitting

- [x] I agree to license this contribution under LICENSE.txt.
- [x] Changed-file pre-commit checks pass.
- [x] Reviewed the applicable AGENTS.md rules; implementation, compatibility and synchronization checks are summarized below. The requested submission scope excludes guide changes and standalone benchmark artifacts.
- [x] GitHub labels: `cat-bugfix`, `area:linear_attention`, `orig-external` (subject to repository permissions).

## Affected area

FE OSS CuTeDSL KDA kernels: local H/M state generation used by Kimi context parallelism, including matching forward and backward recomputation.

## Summary / Why

Keep the BF16 KDA projection accumulator in FP32 through residual subtraction and beta scaling, then round only the resulting Y operand:

```
P_H = K_decay @ H;  Y_H = BF16(beta_fp32 * (V_fp32 - P_H_fp32))
P_M = K_decay @ M;  Y_M = BF16(beta_fp32 * (0      - P_M_fp32))
```

Previously the projection was first rounded to BF16, followed by packed BF16 subtraction/scaling. In cancellation-sensitive cases this can erase the entire residual. The analytic regression uses P = 1 + 1/256, V = 1, beta = 1/2: the old path returns zero instead of the exactly representable correction -1/512.

A register-only helper applies the rule in normal prefill, H/M summary, checkpoint recompute and backward Y regeneration. Backward dBeta retains the unrounded BF16-path residual. Prep-fed prefill only changes subtraction: beta is already folded into the prep records and is **not applied twice**. FP16 retains its existing projection/beta rounding and packed arithmetic.

## Relation to FLA precision staging

| Stage | FLA organization | cuDNN before this fix | cuDNN after this fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| H residual | FP32 accumulator from W @ H; subtract it from u in FP32 before narrowing the residual for the next MMA. | Round the projection to BF16 before residual subtraction and beta scaling. | Keep the projection, residual and beta scaling FP32 until Y packing. |
| M feedback | Build the complete chunk transition A = D - K_restore^T @ W in FP32, then apply A @ M using FP32-typed operands; no matching standalone projection-to-BF16 stage before beta scaling. | Round K_decay @ M to BF16, then form beta * (0 - projection) with packed BF16 arithmetic. | Form the negative-feedback residual/scaling in FP32 before the final Y cast. |

Source comparison: [FLA H projection/subtraction](https://github.com/fla-org/flash-linear-attention/blob/0d0a2f9a5bac74b34b5d2fb4e7192fe85374ea90/fla/ops/cp/chunk_delta_h.py#L124-L147), [residual narrowing](https://github.com/fla-org/flash-linear-attention/blob/0d0a2f9a5bac74b34b5d2fb4e7192fe85374ea90/fla/ops/cp/chunk_delta_h.py#L185-L215), [FLA M recurrence](https://github.com/fla-org/flash-linear-attention/blob/0d0a2f9a5bac74b34b5d2fb4e7192fe85374ea90/fla/ops/cp/chunk_delta_h.py#L269-L298).

These are different algebraic organizations: FLA folds beta and the chunk inverse into W/u, which themselves use low-precision operands/storage. FP32-typed dot operands do not alone establish IEEE FP32 or TF32x3 multiplication. This fix removes the identified early rounding points; it does not claim complete FLA precision parity or change cross-rank merge precision.

## API and compatibility impact

No public signature, shape/stride contract, workspace, launch configuration, architecture/DSL requirement or routing change. MMA operands, chunk inverse, checkpoint representation, collective operations and merge are unchanged.

The patch is based on official develop `0855a16317486492c44b02396309bec8391f6dc7`, not the older preliminary-review baseline. Only **nine implementation/API-doc/test files** are changed; no AGENTS.md or benchmark script/report is submitted.

## H/M accuracy

Fresh A/B against the official baseline above and patched commit `9b0522154ba0029e34227fef00f0321d83b499b4`. The independent reference is a CPU FP64 per-token recurrence, not either revision's serial implementation.

32,768 tokens, two heads, K = V = 128, CPU seed 1731; identical CPU-generated BF16 Q/K/V/beta and FP32 gates/initial state. Long-memory gates are approximately -1e-5 and beta approximately 0.001. Internal piece chains and d_v splitting are disabled **only in the experimental harness** to isolate the local recurrence.

Relative L2 E = norm(X - X_FP64) / norm(X_FP64). The error columns show 100 * E; the reduction column shows 100 * (1 - E_patched / E_baseline).

| Metric | Baseline relative L2 (%) | Patched relative L2 (%) | Relative error reduction (%) | Baseline max abs | Patched max abs |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| H | 0.052656 | 0.039014 | 25.91 | 1.32396e-4 | 9.21678e-5 |
| M | 0.020227 | 0.018590 | 8.09 | 1.19114e-4 | 1.11295e-4 |

Thus H error changes from 0.052656% to 0.039014%, a 25.91% relative reduction—not a 25.91% remaining error. H summary matches ordinary uncut forward final state bitwise for both tested cases (4K standard and 32K long-memory).

The presentation intentionally focuses on H/M. Downstream projected-output error also depends on gating/decay and the particular case; original raw diagnostics are retained, not deleted. These are local synthetic operator measurements, not a distributed CP8, model-loss or training-convergence test. 256K is measured for performance only, not FP64 accuracy.

## Performance

Fresh processes on the same user-specified B300 in A/B/B/A order, two runs per revision. Each cell uses three warm calls, four calls per captured CUDA Graph, three warm replays and 17 timed replays per run; compilation, input preparation and FP64-reference work are excluded. Performance cases use 16 heads. Times are the mean of each revision's two run medians.

| Tokens / D | Operation | Baseline mean of medians (us) | Patched (us) | Time change |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 4096 / 64 | forward_uncut | 157.45 | 158.58 | 0.72% |
| 4096 / 64 | summary_hm_uncut | 187.91 | 189.82 | 1.02% |
| 4096 / 64 | backward_with_recompute | 689.12 | 685.52 | -0.52% |
| 32768 / 128 | forward_uncut | 1682.86 | 1717.63 | 2.07% |
| 32768 / 128 | summary_hm_uncut | 2081.34 | 2104.07 | 1.09% |
| 32768 / 128 | backward_with_recompute | 7983.50 | 8031.33 | 0.60% |
| 262144 / 128 | forward_uncut | 13358.46 | 13632.98 | 2.06% |
| 262144 / 128 | summary_hm_uncut | 16541.83 | 16724.43 | 1.10% |

Positive changes mean longer GPU time. Baseline repeat drift was at most 0.20%. Separate contexts, unlocked clocks and uncontrolled code placement limit interpretation of the small 4K differences; these are operator-stage observations, not model-throughput claims. No 256K backward timing is claimed.

## Testing

User-specified B300, CUDA 13, Torch 2.12.1+cu130. Verified source overlay on the installed compiled extension; this is not a fresh full-package build. Concrete kernel import paths and SHA256 hashes were checked. Persistent FE compiled-cache reuse was disabled for fresh validation.

- New focused GPU suite: **58 passed**. Covers K/V=64/128 intersections, first/steady chunks, BF16/FP32 beta, prep-fed execution, H/M operand packing, legacy FP16 math and saved-checkpoint/recompute backward parity with/without safe gate.
- CI `-k frost` collection includes all 58 cells, exactly 2 L0 / 56 L1, preserving GPU-exclusive and xdist-group markers.
- Existing selected KDA regressions: **28 passed, 7 skipped**, not a full repository run. Includes head dimensions, initial/ragged state, backward gradients against FP64, affine summary, prep and checkpoint paths.
- RED/GREEN on the latest official baseline: the new cancellation smoke test fails before the fix with max absolute correction error 0.001953125, and passes after the fix.
- Changed-file Black/SPDX checks, Python syntax and `git diff --check` pass.
- Test runs exclude root conftest crash-isolation orchestration using `-c /dev/null --confcutdir=<linear_attention[/frost]>`. Existing-suite marker-registration warnings and installed-extension nanobind teardown diagnostics are retained in logs; successful test processes exit 0.

Re-run the focused files from `test/python` with `pytest -m "L0 or L1" -k frost linear_attention/frost/test_kda_frost_fp32_residual.py linear_attention/frost/test_kda_frost_residual_operand.py`.

## Final checks

- **Compatibility audit: passed.** BF16/FP16, beta BF16/FP32, H/M, initial/steady, dimension and prep/recompute intersections checked; no public buffer or fallback contract change.
- **Docstring audit: passed.** Helper packed-word/FP16 contracts, public forward/summary precision notes and all five affected compute roles are documented; 19/19 changed/new top-level functions have docstrings (local AST check, not a claim about a third-party coverage score).
- **Fence audit: passed.** Register-only arithmetic change. Projection-MMA completion before TMEM reads, packed-Y store completion/publication before MMA consumption, and consume-to-reuse/barrier phases are preserved. Exact barrier helper semantics were checked; the synchronization/lifetime call AST is unchanged in each of the five affected kernels. No added broad fence or assumed automatic wait-load.

+    """Return two FP32 residuals for backward dBeta accumulation.
+
+    ``value_word`` packs two values of compile-time ``dtype`` (BF16 or FP16).
+    Supply both FP32 projection components, or omit both for a zero-state
+    projection. BF16 computes V - projection without an intermediate cast;
+    FP16 preserves the legacy rounded projection and packed subtraction before
+    widening the residual. No memory access or cross-thread handoff occurs.

+def cancellation_inputs(dim_k, dim_v, active):
+    """Exactly representable inputs whose FP32 projection is a BF16 midpoint.
+
+    P = 1 + 1/256 rounds to BF16 1, so the old packed subtraction incorrectly
+    produced zero. beta * (V - P) = -1/512 is exactly representable in BF16.
+    Only one token has a nonzero key, isolating initial/steady-state Y staging
+    from inverse approximation and preceding state-rounding errors.
+    """

+    q[..., 0] = 1
+    k = torch.zeros_like(q)
+    k[active, :, 0], k[active, :, 1] = 1, 1 / 256
+    v = torch.zeros(tokens, 1, dim_v, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+    v[active] = 1

+    beta = torch.full((tokens, 1), 0.5, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+    cu = torch.tensor([0, tokens], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    seed = torch.zeros(1, 1, dim_v, dim_k, device="cuda")
+    seed[..., :2] = 1
+    expected = seed.double().clone()
+    expected[..., 0] -= 1 / 512
+    expected[..., 1] -= 1 / 131072
+    return (q, k, v, gate, beta, cu), seed, expected
